The '''Kittât''' (or '''Sith alphabet''') was one of the [[Writing/Legends|writing systems]] used by the ancient [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-wielding]] [[Species/Legends|species]] hailing from [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]] in the [[Stygian Caldera]]. When the [[Exiles|Dark Jedi Exiles]] enslaved the Sith, their [[Sith (language)|language]] and alphabet were recuperated by the newly founded [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]].

==Overview==
Kittât was generally written from left to right in horizontal lines. It consisted of 37 glyphs, including 6 vowels, 2 diphthongs, 17 basic consonants and 12 consonant clusters. Consonants were constructed by the combination of a long vertical stroke and various hooks or barbs. The vowels were indicated by diacritics which appeared above the consonant which preceded. When vowels came at the beginning of a word or stood on their own, the diacritics appeared alone. Besides the uniliteral glyphs, there were also biliteral or triliteral signs, representing compound consonants like ''mw'' or ''tsw''.<ref name="SLS">{{InsiderCite|134|Speak Like a Sith}}</ref>

==Usage==
This variant of Sith writing lent itself to both calligraphy and other uses such as printing and stone carving.<ref name="SLS" /> Some ancient rituals in [[Sith (language)|Sith]], like the ''[[Dwomutsiqsa]]'' ("Summon Demon") were written in this runic alphabet, and so were ritual inscription on [[Sith burial shroud|mummy shrouds]].<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Beyond these and other abstract concepts that appealed to the linguistics wonk in me, there was also a writing system to invent.|Ben Grossblatt|<ref name="SLS" />}}
This alphabet was designed by [[Ben Grossblatt]] for the [[2012]] reference book ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'', but was first identified as Kittât in ''[[Speak Like a Sith]]'', an article featured in the [[Star Wars Insider 134|''Star Wars Insider'' 134]].

Due to its various ecclesiastical uses (such as incantations and ritual writing), the Kittât might in fact be [[High Sith]],<ref name="TWW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref> but neither the ''Book of Sith'' nor ''Speak Like a Sith'' have specified it.
